test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Electrician) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: 20 kVA, 2500/250 V, 50 Hz, single-phase transformer gives an open circuit test result (on the low voltage side) of 250 V and 100 W; what will be the core loss current?
solution:
__**Concept:**__

In an open-circuit test of a transformer, the wattmeter reading represents **core (iron) losses**.

The no-load current has two components:

1) **Core-loss component (Iw)** — in phase with voltage

2) **Magnetizing component (Im)** — lagging by 90°

__**Calculation:**__

**Given:**

Open circuit test on LV side:

Applied voltage, V = 250 V

Core loss (wattmeter reading), P = 100 W

The core-loss current component is:

 I_w = (P)/(V) 

Substituting the values:

 I_w = (100)/(250) = 0.4 A 

**Hence, the core loss current = 0.4 A**
